Rishi — thanks. Answers:  
- Maintenance cadence: We have a weekly maintenance window (Saturdays 02:00–06:00 local) and an extraordinary change process for emergency fixes. For any emergency patches outside the window, we need a documented process and authorization path.
- Backup medium: We'll use a customer-managed NAS with periodic offline snapshots. Assume removable-media transport for DR exercises.
- Operator staffing: We have a site ops team (2 people) plus L2 on-call. We expect Redwood to provide clear playbooks for the site operators.

One more ask: can you provide the exact sequence for applying signed model artifacts and how trust is verified without outbound telemetry? We also need a pointer to any attestations you can provide for reproducible builds.

Subject: Internal: SLA carve-outs & operator-runbook notes for Novapharm

Team — quick notes from product/legal POV as you finalize the external packet:  

SLA carve-outs we should propose (recommended):
- Patch delivery: For air-gapped customers we offer a Time-to-Package SLA (48–72 hours for security-critical patches once validated) but require agreed maintenance windows for installation.
- Remote diagnostics: No outbound telemetry by default; remote troubleshooting requires a secure operator mediation channel (operator initiates a support session or ships diagnostic bundle). This increases MTTR expectations.
- Upgrade assistance: For major upgrades in air-gapped installs we provide operator-assisted orchestrations; full automation not guaranteed.

Operational guidance to include in runbook:
- Explicit step-by-step for KMS offline activation (importing customer keys, local HSM integration notes).
- Signed artifact verification flow: vendor-provided signing key, local verification command set, sample verification script.
- Backup & restore with removable media checklist and integrity verification.

I'll draft a short SLA-exception-draft.docx and loop Legal for tailored language; Laura — can you ensure the legal team is ready to turn our proposed exceptions into contract text?

- Vanessa
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Sarah — attaching the consolidated packet. Highlights inline:  

1) Operator Runbook (attached): installation checklist (preflight), weekly operator tasks, emergency rollback, and DR recovery using removable media. The runbook assumes customer NAS snapshots and two-site operator escalation.
2) Offline KMS & signing: We support customer-managed keys (HSM or KMIP-compatible KMS). The process requires the operator to import signed key material during initial install; subsequent upgrades use signed artifacts and a local verification utility — no outbound traffic required. Steps and example commands are in the runbook.
3) SLA exceptions: Proposed contract language (summary) — Patch-time guarantees of 48–72 hours for validated security patches, with installation within agreed maintenance windows; operator-assisted upgrade model for major releases; higher MTTR for forensic diagnostics unless operator mediation is enabled.

Next steps:
- Please confirm acceptance of the proposed maintenance window approach and whether you want Redwood to include operator-assisted upgrade labor estimates in the contract (we can include up to 16 hours per major upgrade as a billable line item).
- If accepted, we'll coordinate a 60-minute runbook walkthrough with your site ops team next week.

Thanks — attaching runbook and a short FAQ.

Best,
